title: Swap-and-Scale: Hire Signal & Onboard Cookbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook (notes + templates) for a ‘Swap-and-Scale’ approach to hiring, interview scoring, and first-90 onboarding for IC roles (IC2–IC4). Goal: reduce time-to-impact, minimize new hire guesswork, and standardize hire-signal calibration across hiring managers.

Status and usage notes:
- Draft — intended for trial with two upcoming hires (eng and product).
- Use as primary artifact for recruiter + hiring manager sync, share with proposed buddy/mentor before offer.
- TODO: convert key scoring sections into a short form for interviewers (one-pager).

Scope:
Covers: pre-hire hiring signals, interview rubric (behavioral + skills + collaboration), hiring committee scoring, offer acceptance timeline, onboarding week0–week12 micro-rotations, mentor handoff template, and risk/mitigation signals. Not a compensation or benefits doc — link out to comp team pages.

HIGH-LEVEL PRINCIPLES (Swap-and-Scale model):
1) Swap: first 14 days emphasize role-swaps (micro-shadow and micro-ownership) so new hire can demonstrate small win delivering live code/feature or documentation.
2) Scale: by week 6 we expect the hire to own a small service or feature area with defined SLOs (quality + delivery tempo).
3) Signal-driven decisions: promote or escalate based on explicit signals (see Hire Signals).

HIRE SIGNALS (pre-offer & early accept):
- Core signals (required):
  - Problem decomposition: candidate can break a medium-scope task into 3–5 concrete steps within 5–10 minutes.
  - Cross-team empathy: can describe a prior example where they negotiated scope with a PM/designer and reached a tradeoff.
  - Delivery track record: evidence of shipped work (links to PRs, feature writeups, or measurable outcomes).
- Nice-to-have signals:
  - Fast learning examples (short ramp stories), infra/tooling experience relevant to our stack.
- Red flags (immediate):
  - No clear ownership examples, inability to explain tradeoffs, patterns of blaming.

INTERVIEW RUBRIC (single-page scoring model to adopt across interviewers):
Scale: 1 (weak) — 3 (meets bar) — 5 (strong). Use whole numbers.
Sections and sample prompts: 
1) Problem Solving (1–5) — prompt: design the simplest reliable ingest pipeline for a small model-serving microservice. Look for decomposition and constraints.
2) Technical Depth (1–5) — prompt: walk through a bug they fixed that required understanding memory/perf (or equivalent domain question). Look for root-cause and experiments.
3) System Design & Tradeoffs (1–5) — prompt: how would you design caching for prefix-heavy LLM inference? (Look for lat/cost/security tradeoffs).
4) Collaboration & Communication (1–5) — prompt: retell a time they changed stakeholder priorities mid-sprint. Look for negotiation, clarity, follow-up rituals.
5) Ownership & Delivery (1–5) — prompt: describe a shipped feature end-to-end. Look for metrics, rollback plan, and post-launch steps.
6) Culture Add / Values (1–5) — optional: checks for psychological safety behaviors, mentoring, bias-awareness.

Scoring guidance (short):
- 3: Candidate demonstrates expected behaviors and can give concrete examples; answers are credible and coherent.
- 4: Above expectation; candidate anticipates edge cases and shows measurable outcomes.
- 5: Exceptional — strong domain intuition, repeatable patterns, and tangible metrics.
- If any required section is scored 1, hiring manager should discuss before moving forward.

Hiring Committee pass rule (recommended):
- Average of sections >= 3.2 AND no section < 2.
- At least two interviewers (incl. hiring manager) must score >=3 on Ownership & Delivery.

DECISION GATES / TIMELINE TEMPLATE (fast offer flow):
- Day -7 to -3 (sourcing window): initial recruiter screen + shortlist PRs.
- Day 0: recruiter intro + hiring manager pre-brief.
- Day 1–4: on-site (virtual) interviews.
- Day 5: panel calibration meeting (30–45 min).
- Day 6: offer ready; Day 7: verbal offer; Day 10: written offer.
Notes: For priority hires, compress to 48 hours from interviews to panel if committee available.

OFFER CHECKLIST (recruiter + HM):
- Candidate's core signals documented in one-pager (links to PRs).
- Mentor named and briefed.
- First 14-day micro-ship defined (owner, success criteria, backout plan).
- Equipment + access checklist created (VPN, laptop, tools) — link to infra SRE onboarding item.

ONBOARDING: Week0 to Week12 Micro-rotation Plan (swap-and-scale steps):
Pre-Day0 (HR + infra): accounts provisioned, laptop imaged, Slack channels created, buddy assigned.
Week0 (Days 0–7): orientation + shadow swaps
- Day0: 30–60 min welcome w/ people-ops + HM; expectations doc handed off.
- Day1–3: Read-only shadow sessions across 3 core owners (infra, product, ops).
- Day4–7: Micro-ownership task assigned (low-risk change), end-of-week review.
Week2 (Days 8–14): impact sprint (micro-feature)
- Deliver small change that touches production behind a feature flag.
- Daily 15-min standup w/ buddy + HM.
Week3–4: stabilization + learning
- 1:1 deep-dive on architecture, rotations with adjacent teams.
Week5–8: scale ownership
- Owner of small service/feature; measured by two metrics (latency, correctness, CI throughput).
- Biweekly manager check-ins focusing on blockers and career signals.
Week9–12: integrate and mentor
- Expected to ship second scoped feature and pair-mentor a new joiner or intern.

Mentor / Buddy Handoff Template (fill before Day0):
- Mentor name, contact, and 3 earliest commit tasks.
- Week0 goal: introduce 3 runbooks + one small onboarding bug.
- Week2 goal: review PR + merge checklist.
- Notes to mentor: plan 30-min sync every other day first 2 weeks.

RISK SIGNALS & MITIGATION (early trigger list):
- Signals:
  - Missed daily standups without notice for first 10 days.
  - Unable to explain implemented code in PR review.
  - Repeated confusion about team goals (elicits questions rather than action).
- Mitigations:
  - Escalate to HM + people-ops; add extra pairing sessions; create a 2-week recovery plan with measurable checkpoints.

INTERVIEWER QUICK-REFERENCE (copyable snippet for calendar invites):
"Please evaluate: Problem Solving, Technical Depth, Ownership. Score 1–5. Add one short sentence on hire signal and one data point (PR link or ship metric)."

SAMPLE INTERVIEW QUESTIONS (domain-specific prompts to vary by role):
- SWE: "Given a token-caching strategy for an LLM service, how do you ensure coherent KV cache invalidation across scaled replicas?"
- Infra: "Describe a time you debugged GPU memory pressure at inference scale; what tooling and metrics helped?"
- PM: "Walk me through a time you had to prioritize latency vs cost for a paid customer SLA."

POST-OFFER: 14-day micro-ship acceptance criteria (for HM + candidate):
- Micro-ship merged to main behind flag or fully documented runbook created.
- Basic telemetry added (1–2 metrics), smoke tests passing.
- Candidate can demo changes end-to-end in 20 minutes.

EXAMPLES / NOTE-TO-SELF (internal):
- Keep the interview length to 45 minutes; last 10 minutes should be candidate questions + culture fit.
- For remote hires, add an extra async onboarding doc with local infra troubleshooting steps.
- Consider a short 2-page cheat sheet for interviewers that maps examples to scoring anchors.

Outstanding questions (action items):
- Create interviewer one-pager (people-ops owner: Ritu).
- Integrate rubric into Greenhouse scorecards (JIRA HR-4212).
- Pilot this flow with next two hires and capture metrics: time-to-first-merge, time-to-own, 90-day retention indicator.

Appendix: example hire-signal one-pager format (to be attached to offer email):
- Candidate one-liner: role, brief strengths, and primary risk.
- Evidence links: PRs / blog posts / repo snippets (up to 5).
- First-14-day micro-ship description: objective, success criteria, mentor.

-- end of draft --

[notes: keep this intentionally pragmatic and slightly informal. This lives in drive as live doc; move to confluence when stable.]
